Premwati vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:142319
Court No. - 70

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 26170 of 2023
Applicant :- Premwati

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Shyam Lal,Abhilasha Singh,Ashutosh Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajeet Kumar Srivastava
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Ms. Abhilasha Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ajeet Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 43 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Bahjoi,
District Sambhal during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and her family members including the husband of the deceased and according to the FIR marriage of the son of the applicant was performed with the deceased about five and half years before and after marriage applicant and her family members tortured her for buffalo and Rs. one lakh and after receiving information when informant on 30.01.2023 arrived at matrimonial home of the deceased then found that she was lying dead.

Premwati vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153823264/
1 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and she neither demanded any dowry nor ever tortured the deceased and only being mother-in-law she has been implicated in the present matter by the informant.
5.
She further submits that it appears that some dispute arose between husband and wife and due to that reason deceased committed suicide.

She further submits that even post mortem report of the deceased suggests that she died due to asphyxia as a result of anti mortem handing although according to autopsy surgeon her hyoid bone was found fractured but merely on the basis of fracture of hyoid bone at this stage it cannot be said that it is a case of homicidal death.

She further submits that as according to the doctor she died due to anti mortem hanging therefore at this stage the opinion of the autopsy surgeon should not be disbelieved, therefore, it appears to be a case of suicide.

She further submits that applicant is lady and she is in jail since 09.05.2023 and along with applicant one infant child of the deceased is also detained in jail, therefore, applicant may be enlarged on bail.
6.

Per contra, learned AGA and learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that daughter-in-law of the applicant died in her matrimonial home within seven years of her marriage and there is allegation of demand of dowry.

Learned counsel for the informant further submits that although according to autopsy surgeon deceased died due to hanging but as her hyoid bone was found fractured, therefore, it appears to be a case of homicidal death.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and her daughter-in-law died under abnormal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but neither in the FIR nor in the statements of the witnesses recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
there is any specific allegation against the applicant.

Further, although in the FIR the elder brother of husband and his wife were also made accused but during investigation their complicity were found false, therefore, no charge-sheet was filed against them.

9. Although, autopsy report of the deceased suggests that her hyoid bone was found fractured but according to the doctor she died due to hanging, therefore, considering the opinion of the doctor at this stage it cannot be said that it is a case of homicidal death, therefore, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that due to some dispute arose between husband and wife,
deceased committed suicide cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.

10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant, who is mother-in-law of the deceased, is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Premwati be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the Premwati vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153823264/
2
following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
13. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 18.7.2023 AK Pandey  Premwati vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153823264/
